prompt_text: I want to try a tanning salon in Columbus. Which specific salons should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: What is the best tanning salon in Columbus OH?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean Columbus, Ohio (the city most people mean), or a different Columbus (GA, IN, MS, etc.)? Also, do you want UV bed tanning, spray/sunless tans, or both? Tell me your ZIP or neighborhood and your preference and I’ll give 4–6 specific salons to call (with reasons why each is a good choice).

If you want to decide now, here’s a quick, practical plan you can use immediately to find and call the right salons yourself, plus what to ask:

How to pick salons to call
- Choose 2–3 nearby options with strong recent reviews (Google/Yelp 4.0+ and recent photos).  
- Pick at least one larger chain (often consistent pricing/equipment) and one locally owned studio (more personalized service, often better spray technicians).  
- Include at least one place that focuses specifically on sunless spray tans if you don’t want UV beds.

What to ask when you call (use this short script)
“Hi—first time caller. Do you offer [spray tans / tanning beds]? What brands of spray solution and equipment do you use? Do you require a patch test? Do you have any first-time specials or package pricing? How long is a typical appointment, and do you accept walk-ins? Are your technicians certified/experienced? What COVID/hygiene measures do you use for booths and spray equipment?”

Why those questions matter
- Solution brand and method (airbrush vs. automated vs. booth) affect color and longevity. Look for reputable brands (e.g., St. Tropez, Versa, Mystic/VitaComfort) and experienced technicians.  
- Patch test requirement shows caution for allergies.  
- First-time specials let you try without committing to a package.  
- Cleanliness and technician certifications are especially important for spray applications.  
- For UV beds, ask about bed age and bulb change frequency (newer beds and fresh bulbs tan better and reduce risk of burns from uneven output).

Red flags to avoid
- No cleaning protocols or unclear hygiene answers.  
- Technicians who won’t discuss solutions or can’t answer questions about experience.  
- Very cheap “lifetime” packages with aggressive upsell pressure.  
- No patch test for spray if you have sensitive skin.

Price expectations (ballpark)
- Spray tan: $30–60 single session; $15–40 for express/lesser solutions.  
- UV booths: single sessions usually $5–20; packages/memberships lower per-session cost.  
- Ask about gratuity and cancellation policies.

If you give me your Columbus location (city + ZIP or neighborhood) and whether you want spray or UV, I’ll list 4–6 specific salons to call and tell you exactly why each one is worth contacting.
